finding: On default tmpfs the fastest 8-worker copy is a plain per-worker mmap. MADV_HUGEPAGE lands inside that interquartile range. MAP_POPULATE, MADV_POPULATE_WRITE, fallocate, 1 MiB pwrites, one shared mapping, and a per-page touch are slower at 8 workers. The copy's weak efficiency is 0.39 for 16 MiB processes and 0.32 for 64 MiB threads, and the readcon write grows with that copy. fallocate before pwrite is a faster pure ext4 copy and a slower tmpfs copy; putting it in the writer did not lower ext4 end-to-end time, so the writer keeps the existing store.
